title: The MLS Wrap: Messi and Suarez hit form for Inter Miami
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Messi and Suarez hit form for Inter MiamiShareLionel Messi and Luis Suárez showed signs they might be hitting peak form for Inter Miami at just the right time, with the MLS Cup Playoffs in sight.
Most teams have just six games to play before the regular season ends, and Inter Miami will no doubt be a threat in the postseason.

But they are still not the best team in the league currently, or even the second or third-best, as a trio of teams continue to impress week in, week out, in the latter stages of the 2026 season, setting records of their own.
It’s safe to say Inter Miami have been unspectacular as a team in 2026 so far, but with Lionel Messi in their ranks, they are always capable of spectacular moments.
There were a couple of those from himself and Suárez as Inter Miami defeated DC United 4-0.

Messi was not down in the dumps following his emotional retirement from international football during the previous international break, and instead put in a performance that makes you think he’d still have plenty to offer Argentina.
Two old friends just out there enjoying themselves… pic.twitter.com/R0EwANfjTx
Suárez retains the striking instincts that made him the best in the world in his position at one point in his career.
Even as the speed is now gone, for as long as he can reach a canter, he will still score goals in MLS, fool defenders, and get assists, too, as he did for Messi’s first.
Messi’s second, meanwhile, was a reminder that he remains world-class, as he danced past multiple defenders before slotting past the goalkeeper.
It was a first win for Inter Miami’s latest head coach, Kily González, and a first clean sheet in 11 league games.
Danish winger Carlo Holse is the highest-rated player (9.7) of the round after scoring a hat-trick for St. Louis in their Sunday night game against LA Galaxy.

The 6-2 win saw St. Louis continue an unbeaten run that now stretches to 20 games, tying the record for an MLS team in all competitions, joining Red Bull New York, who also managed 20 games unbeaten in 2016.
Holse, 27, joined St. Louis as a designated player this summer and has gradually been introduced to the team over the past two months.

He’s had a run of four starts since mid-September, having mostly been limited to appearances off the bench late in games prior to that, and in these most recent games has scored five goals and registered one assist.
The third goal for his hat-trick this weekend was particularly good, as he did brilliantly to control a long ball from Chris Durkin on his chest before turning and shooting.
Fellow summer signing Rafael Navarro wasn’t far behind him with a FotMob rating of 9.5 thanks to two goals and two assists of his own.
His all-round centre-forward play combined with the runs of Hulse could be a great combination for St. Louis in the playoffs.
Their 20-game unbeaten run also includes wins in the US Open Cup. They’ll face Columbus Crew in the final next week, giving them a chance to have a trophy to show for this impressive form.
A cup win would be good accompaniment to their climb to second place in the Western Conference, where they are now just a point behind Vancouver Whitecaps.
